rules.title: Source-of-income discrimination prohibited in rental housing (FEHA)
rules.requirement: A California landlord cannot refuse to rent to you, or give you different terms such as a higher deposit, because of how you pay rent, including a Section 8 voucher or other rental assistance. If this happens, you can file a complaint with the Civil Rights Department within one year or sue in court within two years.

coverage.summary: Applies to most housing accommodations in California and to most housing providers, including landlords, property managers and tenant screening companies.
minor_exemptions_not_in_data: Owner occupying a home and renting to one additional person may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics (but may not publish discriminatory advertisements)

rules.exemptions: An owner occupying a home and renting to one additional person may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics, but still cannot make, print or publish discriminatory statements, notices or advertisements.
rules.penalty: Remedies include out-of-pocket losses, injunctions, access to the denied housing, emotional distress damages, civil penalties or punitive damages, and attorney's fees.
rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”). This includes the State of California’s COVID-19 Rent Relief Program, Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers, (SSI) social security disability benefits, or wages earned from a job.

rules.title: Limits on use of criminal history in tenant screening (FEHA)
rules.requirement: A California landlord may not consider arrests that did not lead to conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and may not ban everyone with a criminal history. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy, considering the nature and severity of the crime and the time since it occurred.

coverage.summary: Applies to most housing accommodations in California and to most housing providers, including landlords and tenant screening companies.
minor_exemptions_not_in_data: Owner occupying a home and renting to one additional person

rules.exemptions: An owner occupying a home and renting to one additional person is generally exempt from FEHA's applicant-selection rules.
rules.penalty: Remedies include out-of-pocket losses, injunctions, access to the denied housing, emotional distress damages, civil penalties or punitive damages, and attorney's fees.
rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system. Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.

notes: CRD fair housing overview page. Only the source-of-income and criminal-history screening rules are in scope. The page cites FEHA generally, not specific code sections, so no section number was added. The owner-occupant exemption (owner renting to one additional person) is mapped to owner_based_exemption_max_units=1 as an approximation. No other in-scope categories are addressed.
